q-14194.name: Question 1
q-14194.problem: Find $p$ if $-2$ is a root of $f(x)=5{x}^{2}+6x-2p.$
q-14194.worked_solution:
Since  $x=-2$ is a root, we have $f(-2)=0.$ Therefore, we can evaluate the polynomial at $x=-2,$ set it equal to $0,$ and solve the equation for the parameter $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-2)^{2}+6(-2)-2p & =0 \\ 20-12-2p & =0 \\ 8-2p & =0 \\ -2p & =-8 \\ p & =4\end{aligned}
$$

q-14203.name: Question 2
q-14203.problem: Find $p$ if $-2$ is a root of $f(x)=3p{x}^{2}-21px-18.$
q-14203.worked_solution:
Since  $x=-2$ is a root, we have $f(-2)=0.$ Therefore, we can evaluate the polynomial at $x=-2,$ set it equal to $0,$ and solve the equation for the parameter $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3p(-2)^{2}-21p(-2)-18 & =0 \\ 12p+42p-18 & =0 \\ 54p-18 & =0 \\ 54p & =18 \\ p & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-14238.name: Question 3
q-14238.worked_solution:
Since  $x=2$ is a root, we have $f(2)=0.$ Therefore, we can evaluate the polynomial at $x=2,$ set it equal to $0,$ and solve the equation for the parameter $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(2)^{4}+k(2)^{3}-7(2)^{2}-57(2)+6k & =0 \\ 16+8k-28-114+6k & =0 \\ 14k-126 & =0 \\ 14k & =126 \\ k & =9\end{aligned}
$$
